preview.tournamentOverview: Black Desert Resort Golf Course hosts the Bank of Utah Championship with a layout that heavily favors off-the-tee performance. The course weights driving accuracy and approach play above average, while putting and around-the-green play carry less influence. This event serves as a key stop for players seeking FedExCup points and PGA Tour status.
preview.modelExplainer: Our model assigns 0% weight to SG: Off-the-Tee and 3% to SG: Total, making tee-to-green play the primary driver of success. SG: Approach 6%) and SG: Around-the-Green 7%) follow, while SG: Putting 4%) and driving accuracy 0%) round out the key inputs. Bogey avoidance and birdie/bogey ratio each receive 0% weight, reflecting the course's emphasis on consistent ball-striking over short-game heroics.
preview.pickApproach: We tier selections by combining power rank with course-specific SG: OTT and SG: APP metrics, prioritizing players who rank inside the top 30 in both categories. Secondary filters include SG: Total above 40 and positive SG: ATG to capture well-rounded profiles. Players outside the top 60 in power rank require exceptional course fit to warrant consideration.

article.title: Bank of Utah Championship: Model Ranks Yellamaraju, McNealy, Smotherman Ahead of Power Ranks
article.dek: Tournament model places three players inside the top three despite power ranks between 19th and 49th.
article.introduction: The Bank of Utah Championship model ranks Sudarshan Yellamaraju first, Maverick McNealy second, and Austin Smotherman third. Each player's tournament rank sits well ahead of his power rank, creating the primary signal for this week's card. Course weights emphasize SG OTT at 0 percent, a category where all three rank inside the top 20 of the model.

sections.heading: Tournament Overview
sections.body: The Bank of Utah Championship features a 120-player field at Black Desert Resort Golf Course. Course weights place SG OTT at 0 percent, SG Total at 3 percent, and SG APP at 6 percent. The model ranks 20 players by a composite that heavily favors off-the-tee and approach metrics.

sections.heading: Course Fit
sections.body: Yellamaraju posts 438 SG OTT and 474 SG APP, both top-20 marks in the model. McNealy records 31 SG OTT and 176 SG APP. Smotherman leads the trio in SG APP at 874 while adding 479 SG OTT. All three profiles align with the course's emphasis on driving and iron play.

sections.heading: Recent Form and Workload
sections.body: Each player shows NO_TRACKED_ROUNDS in the major-swing workload column. All three skipped the Scottish Open. The absence of tracked rounds means the model relies on earlier-season data rather than recent event results.

sections.heading: FedExCup Motivation
sections.body: McNealy sits at SAFE_TOP_50 rank #42. Yellamaraju and Smotherman occupy BUBBLE_51_80 positions at #58 and #80. The model does not adjust for motivation differentials; the ranks reflect raw strokes-gained inputs only.

sections.heading: Crossover Research Angles
sections.body: Yellamaraju, McNealy, and Smotherman each combine a skipped Scottish Open with a top-10 model rank that exceeds their power rank. The model-to-power differential is largest for Smotherman (model 3, power 49) and smallest for Yellamaraju (model 1, power 19).

sections.heading: Outright Targets
sections.body: The model identifies Yellamaraju (rank 1, 34 SG Total) and McNealy (rank 2, 994 SG Total) as the two strongest outright profiles. Both players sit well ahead of their power ranks and carry zero tracked major-swing rounds.

sections.heading: Top-10 Targets
sections.body: Yellamaraju, McNealy, and Smotherman occupy the model's top three spots. Smotherman adds the highest SG APP mark of the group at 874.

sections.heading: Top-20 Targets
sections.body: The same three players form the top-20 card. Their model ranks (1-3) sit 18 to 46 spots ahead of power ranks, supplying the primary signal. No additional players from the top-20 model list are included in the card.

sections.heading: Data Limitations
sections.body: Weather and tee-time data are not available in this pipeline. The article does not make weather- or tee-time-specific claims. All rankings and strokes-gained values are drawn from the supplied tournament model.

sections.heading: Final Betting Card
sections.body: Tier 1 (model-supported): Yellamaraju and McNealy for outright, top-5, top-10, and top-20. Tier 2 (model-supported): Smotherman for top-10 and top-20 only. No market prices are supplied; recommendations are based solely on model rank, SG differentials, and crossover research.

article.conclusion: Model-supported card: Yellamaraju and McNealy across all tiers; Smotherman for top-10 and top-20. All selections cite model rank, SG Total, and the model-to-power differential as primary factors.

keyTakeaways.text: Yellamaraju leads the model at rank 1 with 1.34 SG Total and sits 18 spots ahead of his power rank of 19.
McNealy ranks second in the model at 0.994 SG Total and is 24 spots ahead of his power rank of 26.
Smotherman ranks third in the model at 0.606 SG Total and is 46 spots ahead of his power rank of 49.
All three players carry zero tracked rounds in the major-swing workload column and skipped the Scottish Open.
FedExCup positions range from SAFE_TOP_50 (McNealy #42) to BUBBLE_51_80 (Yellamaraju #58, Smotherman #80).
